newsitem.title: CHINA: China military goes on high alert after Deng dies.
newsitem.headline: China military goes on high alert after Deng dies.

text.p: China's armed forces have gone on high alert to guard against ethnic unrest and internal instability in some areas after the death last week of paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, Chinese sources said on Sunday.
Defence commanders put their soldiers on first-level alert following Deng's death last Wednesday, said the sources, who are familiar with army affairs.

Members of the three-million-strong People's Liberation Army would be on guard against disturbances in Beijing and in remote regions such as Tibet and Xinjiang that have long been dogged by unrest among native minorities, they said.

In Beijing, soldiers would be standing by in the event of trouble involving large groups of civilians gathering on Tiananmen Square, which in 1989 was the focus of pro-democracy demonstrations crushed by the army with heavy loss of life.
China would likely use police and paramilitary police for initial attempts to control civil unrest, which the military believes to be unlikely, the sources said.
Analysts say China is determined that Deng's death will not be allowed to spark a repeat of the 1989 protests, which were prompted by the death of former senior leader Hu Yaobang.

The army would be ready to react within minutes to any disturbance on the square, which would be under close watch on Tuesday when a memorial service for Deng is held in the neighbouring Great Hall of the People, the sources said.
Troops in such areas as the restive Himalayan region of Tibet and far-northwestern Xinjiang would also be ready to clamp down on any ethnic unrest, they said but gave no details.

Beijing ordered crackdowns on dissent in Tibet and Xinjiang in 1996 to try to crush underground independence movements and end sporadic protests against Chinese rule that have rocked both regions in recent years.

At least 10 people were killed earlier this month in rioting by members of the Uighur minority in the Xinjiang town of Yining. Witnesses said the riots were crushed by paramilitary police, but analysts say tensions in the region still run high.
